subject: biology
title: Pathogens and how disease spreads
key_idea: A **pathogen** is a microorganism that causes disease. Pathogens are bacteria, viruses, fungi or protists. They spread by direct contact, in the air, in food and water, or on a vector, and each route can be blocked.

blocks.text: Some diseases can be passed from one organism to another. This section covers the four types of pathogen and how each one causes harm.

items.meaning: A disease caused by a pathogen that can be passed on, also called an infectious disease.
A disease that is not caused by a pathogen, so it is not passed from person to person.

rows: Reproduce rapidly in the body. May release **toxins** (poisons) that damage tissues and make you feel ill.
Live and reproduce inside cells. This damages the cells.
Infect plants or animals. Many spread as spores.
Rose black spot, barley powdery mildew
Single-celled organisms. Some live in a vector and pass to the host.

blocks.text: Pathogens may infect plants or animals. Bacteria and viruses can reproduce rapidly inside the body, so an infection can get worse quickly.

items: A pathogen is a microorganism that causes disease.
The four types are bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists.
Viruses damage the cells they live in. Bacteria can release toxins.

blocks.text: A pathogen has to get from one host to another. There are four main routes.

items: **Direct contact:** touching an infected person, or exchanging body fluids such as blood. HIV and Ebola spread this way.
**Air:** droplets from coughs and sneezes are breathed in. Measles and tuberculosis spread this way. Fungal spores can be carried by the wind.
**Food and water:** the pathogen is swallowed in food prepared in unhygienic conditions, or in dirty water. Salmonella and cholera spread this way.
**Vectors:** an organism that carries the pathogen from one host to another. Mosquitos spread malaria. Ticks spread Lyme disease.
Fungal spores are spread by wind and water, and enter leaves through the stomata.
Insects that feed on a plant can act as vectors. A virus in tulips is injected into the phloem by feeding insects.
Bacteria can be carried by beetles. In cucumber plants the bacteria block the xylem, so less water reaches the leaves and they wilt.

diagram.alt: Sort each example into the way the pathogen is spread: in the air, by food, water or contact, or by a vector.
diagram.prompt: How is each pathogen mainly spread?

items.text: Measles virus in droplets from a sneeze
Fungal spores blown on the wind
Salmonella bacteria on badly prepared food
HIV in blood shared on needles
Malaria protist carried by a mosquito
Lyme disease bacteria carried by a tick
Plant virus injected by feeding insects

items: The four routes are direct contact, air, food and water, and vectors.
A vector is an organism that carries a pathogen between hosts.
Plant pathogens spread by wind, water and insects.

blocks.text: To stop a disease spreading, block the route it uses. Link each measure to the route it blocks.

items: **Air:** cover your nose and mouth when you cough or sneeze, avoid close contact with infected people, and isolate infected people.
**Food and water:** wash hands after using the toilet and before handling food, do not prepare food while infected, and do not share utensils or towels.
**Contact:** use a condom, do not share needles, and disinfect clothes and surfaces.
**Vectors:** use insecticides or remove breeding sites so there are fewer mosquitos. Use mosquito nets and repellents to avoid being bitten.
**Vaccination:** most people become immune, so fewer people are exposed to the pathogen. Chickens in the UK are vaccinated so fewer bacteria reach food.
Remove and burn infected plants. Clear dead plants from fields so spores do not spread to new plants.
Grow a different crop the next year. Spores left on barley cannot infect wheat, so the fungus dies out.
Spray insecticides to kill insect vectors.
Name the route, then give the measure that blocks it.
Vaccination means most of the population is immune, so there is less chance of a non-immune person meeting the pathogen.
Killing vectors and avoiding bites controls vector-borne disease.

checks.q: State the meaning of the term pathogen.
Describe how the measles virus is transferred from person to person.
checks.a: Coughs and sneezes spread virus in droplets. The droplets are inhaled (breathed in) by another person.

checks.q: Give two methods used to prevent people catching malaria, with a reason why each works.
checks.a: Mosquito nets, to avoid being bitten. Insecticides, to kill mosquitos (the vector). Insect repellent, so people are less likely to be bitten.

exam_phrases: wash hands after using toilet / being sick
is not caused by a pathogen / infective organism

mistakes.wrong: Wash your hands to stop the spread of Salmonella.
mistakes.right: "Wash hands" on its own is ignored. Say when: after using the toilet or being sick, or before preparing or handling food.

mistakes.wrong: Insecticides kill insects, so people do not get malaria.
mistakes.right: "Kill insects" unqualified is ignored. Say insecticides kill mosquitos, the vector.

mistakes.wrong: Measles spreads by contact with an infected person.
mistakes.right: "Contact with infected person" unqualified is ignored. Say coughs and sneezes spread the virus in droplets, which are inhaled.

mistakes.wrong: Social distancing stops the spread of HIV.
mistakes.right: Handwashing and social distancing are ignored for HIV. Say avoid sexual intercourse, use a condom, or do not share needles.

worked_example.question: Pathogens are microorganisms that cause infectious diseases. Give two methods used to prevent people catching malaria. Give a reason why each method works.
answer_points: Method: insecticides. Reason: to kill mosquitos / the vector.
Method: (mosquito) nets. Reason: to avoid being bitten.
Method: insect repellents. Reason: less likely to be bitten.
Method: vaccination. Reason: so people are immune to malaria.
Method: anti-malaria tablets. Reason: kills the pathogen / protist.
worked_example.tip: Any two methods score one mark each, and each needs a correctly linked reason for a second mark.

exam_phrases: avoid close contact with infected people
spread of TB is airborne droplets / TB is spread through the air
so humans are more likely to be bitten

mistakes.wrong: A pathogen is a bacterium such as Streptococcus.
mistakes.right: Examples of pathogens are ignored unless they are linked to causing disease. Say a pathogen is an organism that causes disease.

mistakes.wrong: Lyme disease has increased because there are more chipmunks.
mistakes.right: Complete the chain: more chipmunks means ticks have more food, or there are more ticks, so humans are more likely to be bitten.
Give the precaution and the reason: cough or sneeze into a tissue, or avoid close contact, because TB is spread through the air in droplets.

worked_example.question: Tuberculosis (TB) is a communicable disease. Explain one way that the spread of tuberculosis (TB) can be reduced or prevented.
answer_points: Cough or sneeze into a tissue, avoid close contact with infected people, or avoid cramped living conditions (1), because the spread of TB is by airborne droplets / through the air (1).
OR vaccination / immunisation (1), to provide immunity / reduces the chance of a person getting infected (1).
OR treat infected people with antibiotics (1), which reduces the number of infected people (1).
worked_example.tip: One mark for the measure and one for the linked reason. Regular hand washing, wearing a mask or isolating an infected person are also accepted.

exam_phrases: beetles transmit bacteria to cucumber / plant (by feeding)
wheat is not a host for the fungus

mistakes.wrong: Fungal infections enter a leaf through holes or wounds.
mistakes.right: "Holes in leaf", wounds, roots and stem are ignored. Say the fungus enters leaves through the stomata.

mistakes.wrong: The beetle spreads the disease to the plant.
mistakes.right: "Disease" and "infection" are ignored. Say the beetle acts as a vector and transmits the bacteria.

mistakes.wrong: The sticky substance stops nutrients reaching the leaves.
mistakes.right: "Nutrients" is ignored. The xylem transports water, so less or no water reaches the leaves and the cells lose turgor.

worked_example.question: A bacterium causes a disease in cucumber plants called bacterial wilt. Bacteria causing the disease are found on beetles. The beetles feed on cucumber plants. Inside the plant, the bacteria produce a sticky substance in the xylem vessels. The leaves of the plants then wilt and die. Explain how a beetle feeding on a cucumber plant causes the leaves of the plant to wilt from this disease.
answer_points: Beetles transmit bacteria to the cucumber plant by feeding (the beetle acts as a vector).
Xylem transports water to the leaves.
If the xylem is blocked by the sticky substance, no or less water can reach the leaves.
Cells become flaccid / lose turgor (pressure), or become plasmolysed.
worked_example.tip: Follow the chain in order: transmission, xylem blocked, less water, cells lose turgor.
